title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
author: L. Frank Baum
description: 《绿野仙踪》（原名《奥兹国伟大的魔术师》）是美国儿童文学之父莱曼·弗兰克·鲍姆于 1900 年出版的奇幻童话名篇。本文件收录了全书完整的 24 个章节。故事讲述了堪萨斯州农场小女孩多萝茜和她的小狗托托被一场狂暴的龙卷风卷到了神奇的奥兹国。为了找到重返家园的方法，多萝茜踏上了前往翡翠城的黄砖路。途中她结识了想要脑子的稻草人、想要心脏的铁皮木夫以及想要勇气的胆小狮子。四位伙伴克服重重险阻、战胜西方邪恶女巫、穿过陶瓷国与战树林，最终明白了智慧、爱与勇气一直蕴藏在自己心中的深刻真理。

chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Cyclone
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 1 章：狂暴的龙卷风

paragraphs.en: Dorothy lived in the midst of the great Kansas prairies, with Uncle Henry, who was a farmer, and Aunt Em, who was the farmer's wife. Their house was small, for the lumber to build it had to be carried by wagon many miles. There were four walls, a floor and a roof, which made one room; and this room contained a rusty looking cookstove, a cupboard for the dishes, a table, three or four chairs, and the beds. Uncle Henry and Aunt Em had a big bed in one corner, and Dorothy a little bed in another corner. There was no garret at all, and no cellar—except a small hole dug in the ground, called a cyclone cellar, where the family could go in case one of those great whirlwinds arose.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝茜生活在堪萨斯州辽阔的大草原中央，与做农民的亨利叔叔和做农民妻子的爱姆婶婶住在一起。他们的房子很小，因为建造房子的木材必须用马车运送许多英里。有四面墙、一个地板和一个屋顶，构成了一个房间；这个房间包含了一个看起来生锈的做饭炉灶、一个放盘子的碗橱、一张桌子、三或四张椅子以及床铺。亨利叔叔和爱姆婶婶在一角有一张大床，多萝茜在另一角有一张小床。根本没有阁楼，也没有地下室——除了在地上挖的一个小洞，被称为龙卷风地下室，一旦那些巨大的旋风刮起，一家人可以去那里避难。

paragraphs.en: When Dorothy stood in the doorway and looked around, she could see nothing but the great gray prairie on every side. Not a tree nor a house broke the broad sweep of flat country that reached to the edge of the sky in all directions. The sun had baked the plowed land into a gray mass, with little cracks running through it. Even the grass was not green, for the sun had burned the tops of the long blades until they were the same gray color to be seen everywhere.
paragraphs.zh: 当多萝茜站在门口环顾四周时，除了各侧辽阔灰色的草原外她什么也看不见。没有一棵树也没有一间房子打破向各个方向延伸到天空边缘的平坦乡村的广袤画卷。阳光把耕地烤成了一团灰色，微小的裂缝穿流其中。甚至连草也不是绿色的，因为阳光把长叶的顶端烧焦了，直到它们变成了到处可见的相同灰色。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, a terrible cyclone whirled across the prairie! Uncle Henry rushed to look after the stock, while Aunt Em opened the trap door and climbed down into the storm cellar. Dorothy caught her little black dog, Toto, but before she could follow Aunt Em, the great wind struck the house. The cyclone lifted the small house high into the air, carrying it miles away over the clouds like a toy feather.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，一场可怕的龙卷风在草原上旋转扫过！亨利叔叔急忙去照顾牲口，而爱姆婶婶打开陷阱门爬进了风暴地下室。多萝茜抓住了她的小黑狗托托，但还没等她跟上爱姆婶婶，大风击中了房子。龙卷风把小房子高高抬入空中，像羽毛玩具一样把它运送到几英里外云层上方。

paragraphs.en: The Yellow Brick Road wound onward through the magical countryside of Oz, flanked by sparkling brooks, colorful wild flowers, and strange golden trees. Dorothy tightly held Toto in her arms, her magical Silver Shoes sparkling with every step she took toward their goal.
paragraphs.zh: 黄砖路沿着奥兹国奇幻的乡村继续盘旋，两侧环绕着闪烁的小溪、绚丽的野花与神奇的金树。多萝茜把托托紧抱在怀里，她魔法银鞋在她朝目标迈出的每一步中都闪闪发光。

paragraphs.en: 'No matter how dreary our home in Kansas may be,' Dorothy remarked softly to the Scarecrow, 'we people of flesh and blood would rather live there than in any other country, be it ever so beautiful. There is no place like home.'
paragraphs.zh: '无论我们在堪萨斯的家多么沉闷，'多萝茜对稻草人软软地注意到，'我们血肉之躯的人们宁愿住在那里，也不愿住在任何其他国家（无论它多么美丽）。没有任何地方像家一样。'

chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Council with the Munchkins
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 2 章：与芒奇金人的会面

paragraphs.en: She was awakened by a shock, so sudden and severe that if Dorothy had not been lying on the soft bed she might have been hurt. As it was, the jar made her catch her breath and wonder what had happened; and Toto put his cold little nose into her face and whined piteously. Dorothy sat up and noticed that the house was not moving; nor was it dark, for the bright sunshine came in at the window, flooding the little room.
paragraphs.zh: 她被一声震动所唤醒，那是如此突然与剧烈，以至于如果多萝茜没有躺在软床上她可能会受伤。正因为如此，震动使她屏住了呼吸并好奇发生了什么；托托把它冰冷的小鼻子凑到她的脸上，可怜兮兮地呜咽着。多萝茜坐了起来，注意到房子没有在移动；也不是黑暗的，因为明亮的阳光从窗户透进来，淹没了小房间。

paragraphs.en: She leaped from her bed and with Toto at her heels ran and opened the door. The little girl gave a cry of amazement and looked about her, her eyes growing bigger and bigger at the wonderful sights she saw. The cyclone had set the house down very gently—for a cyclone—in the midst of a country of marvelous beauty. There were lovely patches of greensward all about, with stately trees bearing rich and luscious fruits. Banks of gorgeous flowers were on every hand, and birds with rare and brilliant plumage sang and fluttered in the bushes and trees.
paragraphs.zh: 她从床上跳了起来，托托跟在她脚后跟，跑去打开了门。小女孩发出一声惊呼环顾四周，她的双眼在她看到的奇妙景象下变得越来越大。龙卷风非常温柔地（对于龙卷风来说）把房子降落在一片有着惊人美丽的乡村中央。到处都是可爱的绿草地斑块，庄严的树木挂着丰富甘甜的水果。手边到处都是绚丽的花坛，带着罕见而鲜艳羽毛的鸟儿在灌木与树木里鸣唱盘旋。

paragraphs.en: While she stood looking eagerly at the strange and beautiful sights, she noticed coming toward her a group of the queerest people she had ever seen. They were not as tall as the grown people she had always been used to, but withal they were not very small. In fact, they seemed about as tall as Dorothy, who was a well-grown child for her age, although they were, so far as looks go, many years older.
paragraphs.zh: 当她站在那里急切地看着神奇而美丽的景象时，她注意到有一群她所见过的最古怪的人朝她走来。他们不如她一直习惯的大人那么高，但总的来说他们也不是非常微小。事实上，他们似乎和多萝茜差不多高（按她的年龄多萝茜是一个发育良好的孩子），尽管就长相而言他们要年长许多岁。

paragraphs.en: The Good Witch presented Dorothy with the magic Silver Shoes of the Wicked Witch of the East, who had been crushed under the house, and instructed her: 'Follow the Yellow Brick Road to the Emerald City, where the Great Wizard of Oz will help you return to Kansas.'
paragraphs.zh: 好女巫赠给多萝茜东方邪恶女巫（她已被压在房子下方）的魔法银鞋，并指示她：“沿着黄砖路前往翡翠城，在那里奥兹国伟大的魔术师会帮助你重返堪萨斯州。”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow nodded thoughtfully, his painted face smiling. 'I cannot understand it,' he said. 'If your heads were stuffed with straw like mine, you would all live in the beautiful places and leave Kansas empty. But it is fortunate you have brains, for a brain is the only thing worth having in this world.'
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人深思地点头，画着的脸上笑着。'我无法理解它，'他说。'如果你们的头像我的一样塞满稻草，你们都会住在美丽的地方，把堪萨斯空出来。但幸运的是你们有脑子，因为脑子是世上唯一值得拥有的东西。'

chapters.title: Chapter 3: How Dorothy Saved the Scarecrow
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 3 章：解救稻草人

paragraphs.en: When Dorothy was left alone she began to feel hungry. So she went to the cupboard and cut herself some bread, which she spread with butter. She gave some to Toto, and taking a bucket from the shelf she carried it down to the little brook and filled it with clear, sparkling water. Dorothy was a innocent, good-hearted little girl, and she resolved to prepare for her long journey to the Emerald City.
paragraphs.zh: 当多萝茜独自留下来时她开始感到饥饿。于是她走到碗橱前给自己切了一些面包，抹上了黄油。她给了一些给托托，并从架子上拿了一个水桶提到小溪边装满了清澈闪烁的水。多萝茜是一个纯真、善良的小女孩，她决定为她前往翡翠城的漫长旅程做准备。

paragraphs.en: She walked along the Yellow Brick Road until she stopped to rest beside a cornfield. Perched on a pole in the middle of the field was a Scarecrow, stuffed with straw, dressed in a blue suit, and painted with a comical face. To Dorothy's utter surprise, the Scarecrow winked at her and spoke: 'Good day!'
paragraphs.zh: 她沿着黄砖路行走，直到停在一个玉米田旁休息。栖息在田野中央杆子上的是一只稻草人，里面塞满了稻草，穿着一套蓝色衣服，画着一张滑稽的脸。令多萝茜完全吃惊的是，稻草人向她眨了眨眼并说话了：“美好的一天！”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy helped him climb down from the pole. The Scarecrow explained that he was miserable because he had no brain inside his painted head. 'I don't mind my legs and arms being stuffed with straw,' he said, 'but I hate to be called a fool because I have no brains.' Dorothy invited him to join her journey to ask Oz for a brain, and the Scarecrow happily accepted.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝茜帮助他从杆子上爬了下来。稻草人解释说他很悲惨，因为在他的画头上里面没有脑子。“我不介意我的腿和手臂塞满稻草，”他说，“但我讨厌因为没有脑子而被叫做傻瓜。”多萝茜邀请他加入她的旅程去向奥兹要脑子，稻草人快乐地接受了。

paragraphs.en: The Yellow Brick Road wound onward through the magical countryside of Oz, flanked by sparkling brooks, colorful wild flowers, and strange golden trees. Dorothy tightly held Toto in her arms, her magical Silver Shoes sparkling with every step she took toward their goal.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Road Through the Forest
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 4 章：穿过森林的旅程

paragraphs.en: After a few hours the road began to be rough, and the walking grew so difficult that the Scarecrow often stumbled over the yellow bricks, which were here very uneven. Sometimes, indeed, they were broken or missing altogether, leaving holes that Toto jumped over and Dorothy walked around. As for the Scarecrow, having no brains, he walked straight ahead, and so stepped into the holes and fell at full length upon the hard bricks.
paragraphs.zh: 几个小时后道路开始变得粗糙，步行变得如此困难，以至于稻草人经常在黄砖上绊倒（这里的黄砖极其不平）。有时确实砖块破损或完全缺失，留下了托托跳过、多萝茜绕过的坑洞。至于稻草人，因为没有脑子，他直直往前走，因此踏进坑洞整个人摔倒在硬砖上。

paragraphs.en: It never hurt him, however, and Dorothy would pick him up and set him upon his feet again, while he joined her in laughing merrily at his own mishap. The trees grew thicker and closer together, and the road entered a dark, dense forest.
paragraphs.zh: 然而这从未伤到他，多萝茜会把他拉起来让他重新站立，而他加入她为他自己的不幸愉快地大笑。树木长得越来越密越来越近，道路步入了一片黑暗、密集的森林。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow marvelled at the green leaves, the fragrant blossoms, and the strange calls of forest birds. 'I have so much to learn,' he remarked thoughtfully, 'for my head was only painted yesterday! But if Oz gives me a brain, I shall know as much as any man in the world.'
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人惊叹于绿叶、香气扑鼻的花朵以及森林鸟儿神奇的叫声。“我有那么多东西要学习，”他深思地注意到，“因为我的头昨天才刚画好！但如果奥兹给我一个脑子，我就会和世界上任何男人一样懂得多。”

chapters.title: Chapter 5: The Rescue of the Tin Woodman
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 5 章：拯救铁皮木夫

paragraphs.en: When Dorothy awoke the sun was shining through the trees and Toto was out chasing birds around them. She sat up and looked about her, and there was the Scarecrow, still standing patiently in his corner, waiting for her. 'We must go and search for water,' she said to him. 'What do you want water for?' he asked. 'To wash my face after the dust of the road, and to drink, so the dry bread will not stick in my throat.'
paragraphs.zh: 当多萝茜醒来时太阳正穿透树木照耀着，托托在外面在他们周围追逐着鸟儿。她坐了起来环顾四周，稻草人还在那里，依然耐心地站在他的角落里等待着她。“我们必须去寻找水，”她对他说。“你想要水干什么？”他问。“为了在路的尘土后洗脸，以及喝水，以便干面包不会卡在我的喉咙里。”

paragraphs.en: They walked into the forest and soon heard a rusted groan. Investigating the sound, they discovered a man made entirely of tin, holding an axe raised in the air, frozen completely stiff! 'Oil-can! Oil-can!' rusted the Tin Woodman through his stiff jaws.
paragraphs.zh: 他们步入森林，很快听到了生锈的呻吟声。调查这个声音，他们发现了一个完全由铁皮做成的人，手里举着一把斧头僵硬冻结着！“油罐！油罐！”铁皮木夫穿过他僵硬的双颚生锈地呼喊。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy quickly fetched an oil-can from his cottage and oiled his joints until he could move freely. The Tin Woodman explained that an enchanted axe had severed his limbs, and he had lost his heart when he was replaced piece by piece with tin. 'I want to ask Oz for a heart,' he said, 'for love is the greatest thing in the world.'
paragraphs.zh: 多萝茜迅速从他的农舍拿来一个油罐，给他的关节抹油直到他能自由移动。铁皮木夫解释说一把被施了魔法的斧头砍断了他的四肢，当他被铁皮一块接一块地替换时他失去了他的心。“我想向奥兹要一颗心，”他说，“因为爱是全宇宙中最伟大的东西。”

chapters.title: Chapter 6: The Cowardly Lion
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 6 章：遭遇胆小狮

paragraphs.en: All this time Dorothy and her companions had been walking through the thick woods. The road was still paved with yellow brick, but these were much covered by dried leaves and dead branches from the trees, and the walking was not at all good. There were few birds in this part of the forest, for birds love the open country where there is plenty of sunshine.
paragraphs.zh: 这一切时间多萝茜和她的伙伴们一直穿过密林行走着。道路依然由黄砖铺成，但这些极大地被树上干燥的叶子和枯枝所覆盖，步行一点也不好。森林的这个部分鸟儿极少，因为鸟儿热爱有着大量阳光的开阔乡村。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, a fearsome Lion bounded out from the forest, roaring loudly and knocking over the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman! But when the Lion snapped at little Toto, Dorothy stepped forward courageously and slapped his nose, crying: 'Don't you dare bite Toto! You ought to be ashamed of yourself, a big beast like you biting a poor little dog!'
paragraphs.zh: 突然，一只可怕的狮子从森林里跳了出来，大声咆哮着并撞倒了稻草人与铁皮木夫！但当狮子冲着小托托咬去时，多萝茜勇敢地跨上前去扇了他的鼻子，喊道：“你敢咬托托试一试！你应该为你自己感到羞愧，像你这样的大野兽咬一只可怜的小狗！”

paragraphs.en: The Lion began to weep, wiping his eyes with the tip of his tail: 'I know it,' he sobbed, 'but I can't help it! I am a coward, and whenever there is danger my heart beats fast.' The companions invited him to join their quest to ask Oz for courage, and the Lion gladly accepted.
paragraphs.zh: 狮子开始哭泣，用他的尾巴尖擦着双眼：“我知道，”他抽泣着，“但我没办法！我是个胆小鬼，每当有危险时我的心就跳得极快。”伙伴们邀请他加入他们的寻求去向奥兹要勇气，狮子欣然接受了。

chapters.title: Chapter 7: The Journey to the Great Oz
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 7 章：前往翡翠城的险途

paragraphs.en: They were obliged to camp out that night under a large tree in the forest, for there were no houses near. The tree made a good roof to keep them from the dew, and the Tin Woodman chopped a great pile of wood with his axe and Dorothy built a splendid fire that warmed her and made her feel less lonely.

paragraphs.en: The next day they encountered giant chasms in the earth and fierce Kalidahs—monstrous beasts with bodies like bears and heads like tigers. The Lion roared fiercely to intimidate the beasts, while the Scarecrow instructed the Tin Woodman to chop down a tree to bridge the chasm.

chapters.title: Chapter 8: The Deadly Poppy Field
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 8 章：致命的罂粟花海

paragraphs.en: Our little travelers walked through a carpet of beautiful green grass dotted with brilliant flowers. Soon they came upon a vast field of scarlet poppies. paragraphs.en: Dorothy soon felt her eyes growing heavy, and she sat down among the poppies and fell fast asleep, holding Toto in her arms. The Cowardly Lion also grew drowsy and collapsed onto the grass. 'We must save them!' cried the Scarecrow. The Tin Woodman and Scarecrow, being made of tin and straw, were unaffected by the scent and carried Dorothy and Toto out of the field.

chapters.chineseTitle: 第 9 章：田鼠王后与拯救巨狮

paragraphs.en: While resting outside the poppy field, the Tin Woodman heard a low growl and saw a wild wildcat chasing a little gray field mouse. The Tin Woodman, having a compassionate heart, raised his axe and chopped off the wildcat's head, saving the mouse.
paragraphs.zh: 当在罂粟花海外面休息时，铁皮木夫听到了一声低沉的咆哮，看到一只野猫在追赶一只小灰色田鼠。铁皮木夫有着一颗富有同情心的心，举起他的斧头砍下了野猫的头，拯救了老鼠。

paragraphs.en: The mouse proved to be the Queen of the Field Mice! In gratitude for her life, she summoned thousands of her mouse subjects. The Tin Woodman built a heavy wooden truck, and the mice pulled the slumbering Cowardly Lion out of the deadly poppy field. Dorothy and the Lion awoke safely in the fresh meadow.

chapters.chineseTitle: 第 10 章：城门守护者与绿眼镜

paragraphs.en: At last the travelers reached the high green wall surrounding the Emerald City. They rang the bell at the big gate, which was opened by a short man dressed all in green.
paragraphs.zh: 终于旅行者们来到了环绕翡翠城的高绿墙前。他们按响了大门的铃，大门被一个穿着全身绿色的矮个男人打开了。

paragraphs.en: The Guardian of the Gate unlocked green-tinted spectacles onto their eyes with a golden key, explaining: 'If you did not wear spectacles, the brightness and glory of the Emerald City would blind you.' With their green glasses secured, they stepped into the marvelous city.
paragraphs.zh: 城门守护者用一把金钥匙把绿色调的眼镜锁在他们的眼睛上，解释说：“如果你不戴眼镜，翡翠城的明亮与辉煌会把你刺瞎。”固定好他们的绿眼镜，他们步入了神奇的城市。

chapters.chineseTitle: 第 11 章：奥兹王座室的四大幻象

paragraphs.en: Even with green spectacles, Dorothy and her friends were dazzled by the wonderful Emerald City. The streets were paved with green marble and studded with emeralds. One by one, the travelers were admitted to the grand throne room of Oz.
paragraphs.zh: 即使戴着绿眼镜，多萝茜和她的朋友们也被神奇的翡翠城所眩目。街道铺着绿大理石并镶嵌着翡翠。一个接一个，旅行者们被获准进入奥兹的宏伟王座室。

paragraphs.en: Oz appeared to each in a different terrifying form: to Dorothy, a giant Floating Head; to the Scarecrow, a lovely Winged Maiden; to the Tin Woodman, a terrible Beast; and to the Lion, a ball of Fire. The Wizard refused to grant their wishes until they destroyed the Wicked Witch of the West.

chapters.chineseTitle: 第 12 章：讨伐西方女巫与泼水融化

paragraphs.en: The companions traveled west into the Winkie Country. The one-eyed Wicked Witch of the West spotted them and sent wolves, crows, and Winged Monkeys to defeat them. The Winged Monkeys caged the Lion and damaged the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, bringing Dorothy to the Witch's castle.
paragraphs.zh: 伙伴们向西旅行步入温基国。独眼西方邪恶女巫发现了他们，派狼群、乌鸦和飞猴去打败他们。飞猴把狮子关进笼子并损坏了稻草人与铁皮木夫，把多萝茜带到了女巫的城堡。

paragraphs.en: The Witch made Dorothy work as a kitchen slave and tricked her to steal one of her Silver Shoes. Enraged by the Witch's cruelty, Dorothy picked up a bucket of water and threw it over the Witch! To Dorothy's surprise, the Wicked Witch melted away like sugar, leaving only a brown puddle on the floor.

chapters.chineseTitle: 第 13 章：解救狮子与伙伴重聚

paragraphs.en: Dorothy freed the Lion from his cage and, with the help of the grateful Winkies, repaired the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman. The Winkies presented the Tin Woodman with a silver oil-can studded with jewels.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝茜把狮子从笼子里释放出来，并在无比感激的温基人的帮助下修复了稻草人与铁皮木夫。温基人赠给铁皮木夫一个镶嵌着珠宝的银油罐。

paragraphs.zh: 多萝茜在女巫的碗橱里发现了魔法金帽。一戴上它，她阅读了里面的咒语，召唤了飞猴。她命令飞猴把他们安全飞回翡翠城。

chapters.chineseTitle: 第 15 章：推倒屏风与揭露骗子真相

paragraphs.en: Demanding their rewards, the four friends entered the throne room. When the Wizard attempted to delay again, Toto knocked over a screen in the corner, revealing an old, bald man manipulating ropes and megaphones!
paragraphs.zh: 要求他们的报酬，四位朋友步入了王座室。当魔术师试图再次拖延时，托托推倒了角落里的屏风，露出了一位操纵着绳索和扩音器的秃头老人！

paragraphs.en: 'I am Oz, the Great and Terrible,' said the little man in a trembling voice. 'I am a humbug!' He confessed he was a former balloonist from Omaha who had drifted to Oz in a storm.
